page: Microsoft Azure F32ams_v7 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Famsv7 family. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. There are no bundled local storage drives or GPUs, though the instance is premium storage capable for external block storage attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor delivers top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth (both read and write operations) rank in the top 25%. PassMark database operations also achieve top-tier status, while PassMark memory scores fall into the average range. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference prompt processing with a small 135M model ranks in the top 10%, whereas prompt processing with a medium 7B model registers in the average tier.

The F32ams_v7 offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for applications requiring large memory footprints without the overhead of local storage. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations rely on network-attached premium storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy parallel computing or large-scale AI training. This instance is suited for database operations, memory-intensive web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
